Chinese remainder theorem

Source: R/ntheory.R
crt.Rd

crt(m, v) returns c(x, M) with x %% m[i] == v[i] %% m[i] for every i and M the product of the moduli, or NULL when the congruences are inconsistent; symmetric = TRUE puts x within half of M. Moduli that are not coprime are handled by solve_congruence(), whose arguments are pairs c(remainder, modulus). crt1(m) precomputes for repeated use with crt2(m, v, mm, e, s). symmetric_residue(a, m) maps a in [0, m) to the residue nearest zero.

Usage

crt(m, v, symmetric = FALSE, check = TRUE)

crt1(m)

crt2(m, v, mm, e, s, symmetric = FALSE)

symmetric_residue(a, m)

solve_congruence(..., symmetric = FALSE, check = TRUE)

Arguments

m

Moduli.

v

Remainders.

symmetric

Return the residue nearest zero.

check

Check the result, falling back to solve_congruence().

mm, e, s

Values from crt1().

a

A residue.

...

Pairs c(remainder, modulus).

Value

c(x, M) or NULL; crt1() returns list(mm, e, s).

Examples

crt(c(99, 97, 95), c(49, 76, 65))
#> [1] 639985 912285
solve_congruence(c(2, 3), c(3, 5), c(2, 7))
#> [1]  23 105
symmetric_residue(3, 6)
#> [1] 3
